clues: This city sits on the Gulf coast in far south Texas, right by the line with Mexico. Just past that line stands a town in Mexico, face to face with this city.
This border city was ranked the fifth hottest in all of America one year. Its winters stay warm, but its summers turn hot and sticky.
A boat man named Charles Stillman founded this city in 1848. He had first made his name with a fleet of river boats close by.
Two early war fights took place here, at Palo Alto and at Resaca de la Palma. They were the first clashes of the war with Mexico.
Ships trade with the world through its deep water port, and most folks in town are Hispanic. That mix seals the name for most.
